title: How to use keyboard shortcuts in Canva on Mac: step by step for beginners
metaTitle: How to Use Keyboard Shortcuts in Canva on Mac
description: Learn how to use keyboard shortcuts in Canva on Mac, with Command key combos for undo, duplicate, group, align and layers, plus fixes.
targetKeyword: how to use keyboard shortcuts in canva on mac
intro: To use keyboard shortcuts in Canva on Mac, hold Command (⌘) with a letter, such as ⌘Z to undo or ⌘D to duplicate, while the canvas is active. Check the menu bar for the exact key, because third-party lists can be out of date, and use T, R, L and C to add objects when you are not typing.
tldr: Most Canva Mac shortcuts start with Command (⌘). Hold it with a letter, like ⌘D to duplicate.
Shift (⇧) changes a shortcut. ⌘G groups, ⌘⇧G ungroups and ⌘⇧L aligns left.
Single keys T, R, L and C add a text box, rectangle, line or circle when you are not typing.
If a shortcut does nothing, check the menu bar, your keyboard layout and any other app using the same keys.

blocks.text: Canva's download page says the Mac desktop app runs on Macs with Intel and Apple chips. The steps here work on either kind of Mac. Where a step depends on the desktop app, this guide says so.
Mac modifier keys for Canva shortcuts
A Mac shortcut is a set of keys pressed together. Apple calls the first keys modifier keys. Menus print a symbol for each one next to the command, so learn the symbols once.

blocks.text: Apple also lists Fn or Globe as a modifier. Apple notes that shortcuts can vary by language and keyboard layout. Check your layout first if a shortcut does the wrong thing.
The most-used Canva keyboard shortcuts on Mac
Undo, duplicate, group and bold cover most small fixes in a design. Start with ⌘Z. Press it after any change you did not mean to make. It is the fastest way to recover.

blocks.text: Where these Canva shortcuts come from

Canva's own help center could not be checked while this guide was written. The table above comes from ShortcutRef, a third-party reference. That list does not show a version or date. Treat it as a starting point, not a final word.

blocks.title: Check the menu bar
blocks.text: The menu bar in your copy of Canva shows the commands it actually has. If a key does nothing, look for the command there first. Apple gives the same advice for every Mac app.
Single-key Canva shortcuts for adding objects
Single-key tools are the fastest way to start a layout. ShortcutRef lists four for Canva on Mac. Each one adds an object with a single key press.

items: T adds a text box
R adds a rectangle
L adds a line
C adds a circle

blocks.text: These keys only work as tools when you are not typing. If a letter appears where you expected a shape, a text box probably had focus. Click an empty part of the canvas and press the key again.
Canva align and layer shortcuts on Mac
Alignment has its own Shift set. ⌘⇧L aligns to the left, ⌘⇧C to the center and ⌘⇧R to the right, according to ShortcutRef. Select the elements first, or the command has nothing to work on.
For layers, ⌘] brings the selected element forward and ⌘[ sends it backward. Think of the square brackets as up and down. The right bracket lifts an element. The left bracket drops it.
The shortcuts handle the basic edges. For more options, read our [align guide](/how-to/align-elements-in-canva).

Superhuman's blog quotes developer Bruno Michels. He estimates that people can waste about 134 hours, or 17 work days, by using the mouse where a keyboard command would work. That is a projection from one developer, not a survey.
The same post says a keyboard cut and paste can save up to five seconds each time. Five seconds sounds small. Multiply it by every copy and paste you do in a week, and the total grows fast.
Worked example: a flyer built with keyboard shortcuts
Say you are making a simple event flyer. Start with a blank design. Build it in the order below, and check the result after each key. Each step uses one shortcut, so mistakes are easy to spot.

items: Press T and type the event name. Press ⌘B to bold it.
Press T again for the date. Type it, then click an empty part of the canvas.
Press R for a rectangle. Select it and press ⌘[ until it sits behind the title.
Select the title and the date, then press ⌘⇧L to line them up on the left.
Select everything you want to keep together, then press ⌘G to group it.

blocks.text: The most common mistake is pressing a formatting key with nothing selected. ⌘B has nothing to bold when no text is chosen. Select first, then press the key. Check the result after each key, not at the end.
Create a custom Mac shortcut for Canva
Not every menu command has a shortcut. macOS lets you add one for any app, including Canva. The shortcut works by matching the menu title, so the wording has to match what the menu shows.

items: Open the Apple menu, then System Settings.
Select Keyboard in the sidebar. You may need to scroll to find it.
Click Keyboard Shortcuts, then select App Shortcuts.
Click Add, then choose Canva from the Application pop-up. You can also choose All Applications.
Type the menu title exactly as the app shows it. Apple says to include the '->' separator and three full stops for an ellipsis.
Press the key combination you want. Each key can be used only once in a combination.

blocks.text: If your new shortcut conflicts with an existing one, it will not work until one of them changes. Check for conflicts right after you add it, so you know the shortcut is live.
Canva shortcuts not working on Mac: causes and fixes
Most dead shortcuts come from a short list of causes. Work through them from the simplest. Start with focus and layout before you reinstall anything.

items: A text box is in edit mode, so the keys type letters instead of acting.
Another app uses the same key combination.
A browser or browser extension overrides Canva's command.
Your keyboard layout does not match the one you type with.
The app is out of date, or the connection is unstable.

blocks.text: One troubleshooting guide for Canva advises testing in incognito mode, which helps isolate extensions. Turn extensions off one at a time and retest after each. It also recommends a connection of at least 5 Mbps.
Fix conflicts with other apps on Mac
Apple's conflict steps work for any app. Open System Settings, select Keyboard, then click Keyboard Shortcuts. Pick a category and look for the warning icon next to a conflicting shortcut.
Double-click the shortcut, then press the new key combination. Keep a note of what you changed. It saves time when a key behaves differently on the next Mac you use.
Keep Canva updated for shortcuts that work

Canva may disable app versions older than six months, or sooner if a critical bug or vulnerability is found. If designs stop opening, check for an update first. The Mac guide by Lilach Bullock lists the same first step.

The Mac guide mentions an Update App button. For install and update steps, follow our [download and install guide](/how-to/download-and-install-canva-in-canva). Canva's download page does not list a minimum macOS version, so the app's own update screen is the best place to check.
Last resort: reset the Canva desktop app

The Mac guide's troubleshooting order ends with a reset. Try the same feature in a browser, update the app, then update macOS before you reset. Save your work first, since force quit can lose unsaved changes.

A reset means deleting Canva-related folders in ~/Library in Finder while keeping the app itself. Read the full reset steps before you start, because you are deleting files. Our [reset guide](/how-to/reset-the-desktop-app-in-canva) walks through it.
Common mistakes with Canva shortcuts

items: Typing a letter in a text box, then wondering why no shape appeared.
Trusting a shortcut list without checking the menu bar.
Mixing up ⌘G and ⌘⇧G. Shift turns grouping into ungrouping.
Blaming Canva for a browser shortcut that fired first.
Changing a system shortcut that another app depends on.

blocks.text: A simple habit prevents most of these. Click the canvas, select the object, press the key, then check the result before you press a second key.
What to do next
Once the core keys feel natural, move on to the tasks they support. Duplicating a design, grouping elements and locking them are good next steps. Each has its own guide.

Read [how to duplicate a design in Canva](/how-to/duplicate-a-design-in-canva), [how to group elements in Canva](/how-to/group-elements-in-canva) or [how to lock an element in Canva](/how-to/lock-an-element-in-canva). Our [Canva guide for designers](/for/designers/canva) covers resizing and exporting.
Pick one new shortcut a day and use it until it feels automatic. Two or three keys are enough to start.

faq.question: Are these the official Canva shortcuts?
faq.answer: Not verified. The list comes from ShortcutRef, a third-party reference, and Canva's own help center could not be checked for this page. The menu bar in your copy of Canva shows the commands it actually has, so trust that first.

faq.question: Why does ⌘Z not undo anything in Canva?
faq.answer: First click an empty part of the canvas, so Canva has focus and no text box is in edit mode. Then look for Undo in the menu bar. If the key still does nothing, work through the causes list in this guide.

faq.question: Do Canva shortcuts on Mac use the Control key?
faq.answer: The shortcuts in this guide use Command (⌘), often with Shift (⇧). Apple lists Control (⌃) as a Mac modifier, but none of the keys in this guide use it.

faq.question: Can I change Canva's built-in shortcuts?
faq.answer: This guide does not show a way to edit Canva's built-in keys. You can add an app shortcut for a menu title in System Settings. It works only when the title matches the menu exactly.

faq.question: Why do letters type instead of adding a shape?
faq.answer: A text box is probably active. Click an empty part of the canvas to leave it, then press T, R, L or C again.

faq.question: Do these shortcuts work with Canva in a browser?
faq.answer: Most of them should, but a browser can use the same keys first. Test in incognito mode, turn extensions off one at a time, and update the browser and macOS.

faq.question: Does the Canva Mac app run on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: Canva's download page says the desktop app is available for Macs with Intel and Apple chips. The page does not list a minimum macOS version.

faq.question: How much time do keyboard shortcuts save?
faq.answer: One developer's model estimates about 134 hours, or 17 work days, lost to mouse use. The same source says a keyboard cut and paste can save up to five seconds. These are projections, not survey results.

faq.question: Why did a shortcut stop working after an update?
faq.answer: Check the menu bar first, because commands can move or change. Then check your keyboard layout. If it still fails, save your work and follow the reset steps further up this page.

task: Use Canva keyboard shortcuts on a Mac
appliesTo: Canva on Mac: desktop app and Canva in a browser, Intel and Apple chip Macs
requirements: A Mac with a Command (⌘) key on the keyboard
Canva open in the desktop app or in a browser tab
A design open with at least one element on the canvas
Keyboard set to the layout you type with
Access to System Settings if you want to add a custom shortcut

steps.name: Check your keyboard layout
steps.text: Open Keyboard settings in System Settings. Apple says shortcuts can vary by language and keyboard layout. Make sure the layout matches the keys you type with.
steps.tip: Check this first if a shortcut seems to fire the wrong command.

steps.name: Open your design and click the canvas
steps.text: Open the design in the Canva desktop app or in a Canva browser tab. Click an empty part of the canvas. Shortcuts act on the design when nothing is in text edit mode.
steps.tip: If you are typing, click outside the text box first.

steps.name: Undo and redo a change
steps.text: Press ⌘Z to undo your last change. ShortcutRef lists Redo as ⌘Y. Test both on a practice design so you know they respond on your Mac.
steps.tip: If ⌘Y does nothing, look for Redo in the menu bar.

steps.name: Duplicate a selected element
steps.text: Click an element to select it. Press ⌘D to make a copy. Move the copy away from the original before you edit it, so you do not change both by accident.
steps.tip: Duplicate first, then edit. It keeps the original safe.

steps.name: Group and ungroup elements
steps.text: Select two or more elements. Press ⌘G to group them, so they move together. Press ⌘⇧G to ungroup them again.
steps.tip: Shift is the difference between the two. Without it, you get the group command, not the ungroup command.

steps.name: Bold selected text
steps.text: Select the text you want to change. Press ⌘B to make it bold. Press ⌘Z to undo it if you change your mind.
steps.tip: Select the text first. With nothing selected, there is nothing to bold.

steps.name: Add text, a rectangle, a line or a circle
steps.text: Click the canvas so no text box is in edit mode. Press T for a text box, R for a rectangle, L for a line or C for a circle.
steps.tip: These keys type letters when a text box is active, so click the canvas first.

steps.name: Align elements to the left, center or right
steps.text: Select the elements you want to line up. Press ⌘⇧L to align left, ⌘⇧C for center or ⌘⇧R for right. For other alignment options, use our [align guide](/how-to/align-elements-in-canva).
steps.tip: Shift is part of every alignment key. Check the result before you move on.

steps.name: Bring an element forward or send it back
steps.text: Select an element. Press ⌘] to bring it forward. Press ⌘[ to send it backward.
steps.tip: Use this to put a photo behind a text box, or a text box in front of a shape.

steps.name: Search Canva and add a link
steps.text: Press ⌘F to search Canva. Select the item you want to link, then press ⌘K to add a link.
steps.tip: Check the link before you share the design.

steps.name: Save and present your design
steps.text: Press ⌘S to save. When the design is ready to show, press ⌘⌥P to present it. Test the presentation once before you share it.
steps.tip: Save first, so the version you present is the version you saved.

steps.name: Make the Canva interface larger
steps.text: If the Canva window is hard to read, go to View > Interface scale > Make larger. This changes the interface size. It does not change the elements in your design.
steps.tip: Use Reset to Default under the same menu to go back.

steps.name: Add a shortcut for a menu command
steps.text: If a Canva menu command has no shortcut, add one in macOS. The shortcut must match the menu title exactly. The full steps are in the custom shortcut section of this guide.
steps.tip: Each key can be used only once in a combination, so pick a new combination.

troubleshooting.fix: Click an empty part of the canvas and try again. Then check the keyboard layout in System Settings > Keyboard, since Apple says layouts can change shortcuts.

troubleshooting.problem: Letters type instead of creating a shape
troubleshooting.fix: A text box is in edit mode. Click outside it on the canvas, then press T, R, L or C again.

troubleshooting.problem: A browser shortcut fires instead of Canva's
troubleshooting.fix: A browser can override Canva's commands. Test in incognito mode, then turn extensions off one at a time. Update the browser and your Mac.

troubleshooting.problem: Another Mac app uses the same keys
troubleshooting.fix: Open System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts. Look for the warning icon, double-click the shortcut and press the new keys.

troubleshooting.problem: Designs stop opening or the app feels broken
troubleshooting.fix: Canva may disable app versions older than six months. Check for an update first. Follow our [download guide](/how-to/download-and-install-canva-in-canva) to update.
Test on a stable connection of at least 5 Mbps. If it persists, save your work and follow our [reset guide](/how-to/reset-the-desktop-app-in-canva).
